notes.claim: Multiplying a function by a positive constant stretches or compresses its graph vertically.
Multiplying all outputs by minus 1 reflects the graph about the x-axis.
A transformation of the form -g(2x) is a reflection in the x axis together with a horizontal compression by a factor of 2.

sources.title: 1.2: 1.2 Graphical Transformations - K12 LibreTexts
sources.quote: This transformation is a vertical reflection across the x axis and a horizontal compression by a factor of 2.

sources.title: 1.5 Transformation of Functions - Precalculus 2e | OpenStax
sources.quote: When we multiply a function by a positive constant, we get a function whose graph is stretched or compressed vertically in relation to the graph of the original function.

sources.title: 1.5 Transformation of Functions - Precalculus 2e | OpenStax
sources.quote: Multiply all outputs by –1 for a vertical reflection. The new graph is a reflection of the original graph about the x -axis.
